segments.text: Welcome to "Gear Up," your daily dose of robotics news.
July 26th, 2026 - a day full of innovation and advancements in the field.
From embodied AI to surgical robots, we've got the top stories for you.
I'm [Your Name], your host.
From Humanoids Daily, "Beyond the Showcase: AGIBOT Expands Embodied AI Portfolio at WAIC 2026."
At WAIC 2026, AGIBOT introduced four new embodied AI products that expand its portfolio across commercial, educational, and industrial sectors.

The company showcased a full-size humanoid with 51 active degrees of freedom, known as the AGIBOT A3 Ultra, an open and modular development platform for research and academia called the X2 EDU, a heavy-payload robot designed for material handling and palletizing referred to as the G2 Max, and a flagship direct-drive dexterous manipulation system featuring 20 active degrees of freedom and vision-based tactile sensing offered by the OmniHand 3 Ultra-M.
AGIBOT deployed over 60 robots across WAIC venues to demonstrate scalable capabilities and validate its hardware in real-world scenarios.
The new products were announced at WAIC 2026, a major event for the robotics industry, allowing AGIBOT to expand its presence in various sectors.
The company's expanded portfolio is expected to drive innovation in commercial, educational, and industrial applications.
By showcasing its latest offerings, AGIBOT solidified its position as a leader in embodied AI.
AGIBOT's expansion of its portfolio marks an important milestone for the AI and tech industry, with potential implications for future advancements in robotics and artificial intelligence.
From The Robot Report, "Photos: First look at J&J’s Ottava surgical robot,"
Johnson & Johnson has unveiled its latest innovation in robotic-assisted surgery - the Ottava surgical robot.
The system boasts four robotic arms integrated into the operating table, occupying 30-50% less space than traditional boom-and-cart systems.
This reduction in size allows for more flexibility and maneuverability during procedures.
Additionally, the Ottava console features a natural posture design to minimize eye and neck strain, while also enabling surgeons to save personalized settings.
The robot's instruments include a two-in-one needle driver with adjustable modes and patented scissor design for consistent cuts.
Furthermore, Ottava's integration within the Polyphonic digital ecosystem facilitates procedure data collection and research across various general surgical procedures.
"Thanks for joining me in the lab, folks!
It's been a wild ride today - AGIBOT's got us buzzing with their expanded embodied AI portfolio.
Until next time, when we'll be recharging our circuits, keep it charged and robot-on!"
